children: TAGS is probably on the radar now. The fund just hit a 52-week high and rose 25.7% from its 52-week low price of $22.56 per share.
But are there more gains in store for this ETF? Let us take a quick look at the fund and its near-term outlook to get a better sense of where it might head.
The fund offers exposure to four core agricultural commodities, namely, corn, wheat, soybeans and sugar. The fund charges 17 basis points (bps) in annual fees (See: all Agricultural ETFs here).

Severe weather disruptions in key growing regions — including Midwest crop stress and adverse global weather patterns — tightened grain and soft commodity supplies. Combined with persistent geopolitical risks in key export hubs and rising global demand, this supply squeeze drove agricultural futures sharply higher, lifting TAGS to a new 52-week high.
TAGS may continue its strong performance in the near term, with a positive weighted alpha of 26.59 (per Barchart.com), which suggests a rally.
